definitions.explanation: A weapon that derives its destructive force from nuclear fission reactions.

examples.japanese: {原子爆弾|げんしばくだん}が{投下|とうか}された。
{原子爆弾|げんしばくだん}の{被害|ひがい}は{甚大|じんだい}だった。
examples.english: The damage from the atomic bomb was enormous.

examples.japanese: {広島|ひろしま}と{長崎|ながさき}に{原子爆弾|げんしばくだん}が{落|お}とされたのは1945{年|ねん}のことだ。
examples.english: It was in 1945 that atomic bombs were dropped on Hiroshima and Nagasaki.

notes:
Usually abbreviated to {原爆|げんばく} in everyday usage. The full form {原子爆弾|げんしばくだん} tends to appear in formal or historical contexts. As the only country to have experienced nuclear attacks, Japan has a deep cultural relationship with this word and its abbreviation.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {原子爆弾|げんしばくだん}を{投下|とうか}する: to drop an atomic bomb
- {原子爆弾|げんしばくだん}の{開発|かいはつ}: atomic bomb development
- {原子爆弾|げんしばくだん}の{被害者|ひがいしゃ}: atomic bomb victims

RELATED WORDS:
- {原爆|げんばく}: atomic bomb (abbreviation) — the more commonly used short form
- {被爆者|ひばくしゃ}: atomic bomb survivor — a word with deep significance in Japanese society
- {核兵器|かくへいき}: nuclear weapons — the broader category that includes both atomic and hydrogen bombs
- {水素爆弾|すいそばくだん}: hydrogen bomb — a more powerful type of nuclear weapon
